draft.title: The demographic transition model
card: The demographic transition model (DTM) shows how birth rates and death rates change as a country develops. Population change depends on the gap between the two rates.

Stage 1: birth and death rates are both high, so population stays low and steady. Stage 2: death rates fall, because of better food, health care and clean water, but birth rates stay high. Population grows fast.
Stage 3: birth rates begin to fall, so the gap narrows and growth slows. Stage 4: birth and death rates are both low, so population levels off.
Birth rates fall later than death rates because family habits and beliefs about family size change slowly. Some versions of the model add a fifth stage, where birth rates fall below death rates.
draft.remember: Death rates fall first and birth rates follow later, so growth is fastest in between.

a.q: Why does a country's population grow fastest in Stage 2 of the model?
opts: Death rates have fallen but birth rates are still high
Birth rates have risen above death rates in a rich country
Both birth rates and death rates have fallen to low levels
Death rates are high but more people are moving in
a.why: In Stage 2 better food, health care and clean water cut deaths, but birth rates stay high, so the gap is wide. In Stage 4 both rates are low, so the gap is small and growth is slow.
a.clue: Look at the gap between the two rates.

b.q: Country X has a low birth rate and a low death rate, and its population is no longer growing quickly. Which stage is it in?
opts: Stage 4, because both rates are low and the gap is small
Stage 2, because death rates have fallen and births are high
Stage 3, because birth rates are still high but falling
Stage 1, because the population is not growing quickly
b.why: With both rates low, the gap between them is small and the population levels off, which is Stage 4. Stage 1 also has slow growth, but there both rates are high, not low.
b.clue: Slow growth happens in more than one stage. Check the size of each rate.

a.best: Death rates have fallen but birth rates are still high

b.best: Stage 4, because both rates are low and the gap is small
